items.paraphrase: A graduated quadrant instrument measures heights and distances; it spans ninety degrees.
items.inference: The singular VI instrument shares the earlier plural V instrument meaning; source pinnules establish sighting use.

items.paraphrase: Pierced sighting plates on an alidade serve surveying observations.
items.inference: The source’s instrument parts are sighting vanes, not magnifying lenses or fern leaflets.

items.paraphrase: Station includes a temporary halt in a location.
items.inference: Surveying observation positions follow from the source instrument and successive two/third positions; the retrieved historical definition does not explicitly name surveying.

items.paraphrase: A person who knows or studies physique.
items.inference: The reasoner’s surveying and geometrical study select natural science, not treating a patient. Historical field scope is supported separately by physique.

items.paraphrase: Science directed at natural things, within philosophy.
items.inference: This supports translating this scene’s physicien as a natural philosopher without imposing a modern disciplinary specialization.

items.paraphrase: Doctor names a holder of the highest university degree and can also name a learned person.
items.inference: The title before Swift in this literary allusion selects a learned academic title rather than medical treatment; no university or degree date is asserted.

items.paraphrase: A figurative relative-comparison use accompanies the presence meaning.
items.inference: The repeated size analogy selects comparison to the still larger substances, not the physical front of them.

retainedHolds: The historical passive-agent en and combined qu’auraient routing remain unreconciled; general de-reference or tense similarity alone does not authorize a learner identity.
